title: Caregiver hand hygiene checklist
category: Medical and first · Aid · Disaster · Health
summary: Medical-heavy survival entry for when to clean hands before and after care, food, toilet, wounds, masks, and waste.
content: Use this entry to organize when to clean hands before and after care, food, toilet, wounds, masks, and waste. Start with scene safety, hand hygiene, calm communication, and written timing. Keep the person comfortable, protect privacy, avoid risky experiments, and prepare a clear handover for a doctor, ambulance, clinic, pharmacist, or trained first-aider. Watch especially for: no soap, shared towels, blood contact, diarrhea care, wound care, or food prep after care. In a long emergency, review the person regularly instead of assuming they are stable.
warnings: Escalate urgently if you see: no soap, shared towels, blood contact, diarrhea care, wound care, or food prep after care.
failure_signs: Red flags appear: no soap, shared towels, blood contact, diarrhea care, wound care, or food prep after care
